function: Excluded (function): the learned KSGAN discriminator only detects adversarial range-Doppler maps (AML attack detection, p. 11); no beams, waveforms, or resources are learned.
notes: Reason function. The only learned component is the KSGAN discriminator (convolution and max pooling blocks, p. 10) that decides whether a received range-Doppler map is genuine or adversarial: p. 11: "tasked with detecting whether there is an AML attack". This is a security detection function, close to the excluded physical-layer authentication and anti-jamming, and it is not one of the seven areas. The switch between ISAC and communication-only transmission, the sensing power share alpha_sen* in {0.5, 0}, and the sensing beam gate alpha_beam are fixed threshold rules on the detector output and on the 2D CFAR result (Eqs. 22-23, p. 11; Eq. 25, p. 12), not learned. BORDERLINE: the abstract (p. 1) frames the adaptive transmission as ISAC resource allocation: "To optimize resource allocation in ISAC systems, we propose an adaptive signal transmission method", so the reviewer may reconsider area 5. Facts for that case: 2 Tx and 2 Rx antennas at the vehicle, 2 or 6 single-antenna users, 77 GHz, no RIS (Table II, p. 13); custom MATLAB and IBM ART simulation of 3000 legitimate range-Doppler maps, no 3GPP channel, no code link (p. 13); no complexity figure reported.
